card.hook: Picture waiting for your flight with a jet rolling past right in front of you, close enough to feel like part of the trip. That's the Terminal B terrace at Punta Cana airport, and it's a great travel-day photo.
card.stand_here: Stand on the outdoor terrace in Terminal B, near gates B25 and B26, and face the taxiway. The terrace is inside the terminal, after security.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for planes passing close, with the gate area in the frame. Try zoom 2x or 5x for planes further along the taxiway (higher zooms depend on your phone). Only use zoom 0.5x if you want the whole gate front, because it makes planes look small and a bit stretched.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the plane, then slide the picture a little darker so the sky doesn't turn white and the plane keeps its detail.
card.best_time: Winter is best here because the light is nicer. In summer the afternoon light comes from behind the planes, so your photos come out backlit.
card.selfie_here: Try the terrace at the far end of Terminal B, beside gates B25 and B26, facing the taxiway. Use the front camera and keep the terminal behind you. The Terminal B welcome sign is another known photo stop, though we can't say for sure that the airport building shows up behind it.
card.rules_and_safety: You need a boarding pass to reach the terrace, as it's after security. Follow any instructions from airport staff, and check the official airport site first because photo rules can change.
card.challenge: Fire off a quick burst as a plane glides past, then pick the frame where it has the most room to 'move' in front of it.
card.good_to_know: Punta Cana International Airport opened in December 1983 and was the first privately owned international airport in the world. Its open-air terminals have roofs covered in palm fronds. Terminal B, opened in November 2014, is the fully enclosed modern one with jet bridges. The airport is now the busiest in the Dominican Republic, with more than 8.3 million passengers in 2022.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the outdoor terrace in Terminal B, near gates B25 and B26, and face the taxiway. The photo isn't taken at the phone icon. The terrace is inside the terminal, after security.

selfie_research.notes: Sources are thin. The only page naming a photo spot at the airport itself is the Terminal B welcome-sign caption, and no page says where a passer-by should stand to frame the visitor with the whole terminal, so ask_someone_spot is null. The terrace spot comes from a plane-spotting guide written for aircraft photos, not tourist selfies; it is airside, so the guide says access requires going through passport control, and a boarding pass is needed. The terrace is also described as having a glass barrier. The Tripadvisor 'Punta Cana sign' is a town sign, not an airport one, so I excluded it. A Wikimedia category lists a 'Courtyard Wall at Punta Cana Airport' and an Instagram-style video describes a stone welcome wall, but no page gives its location, so I did not use it. A Tripadvisor forum says photo staff used to pose arriving passengers near the terminal entrance for a fee, and an Airial page says aircraft photography is generally allowed but to follow posted guidelines; neither is a selfie-stick or tripod rule, so no rules were reported. The Terminal B welcome sign's suitability for a selfie with the airport behind it is unconfirmed.

card.hook: Picture water so calm and glassy that the catamarans anchored offshore seem to float on a mirror. That's Playa Juanillo, and it's the best place to start Cap Cana, which is a big place.
card.stand_here: Stand on the shoreline of Playa Juanillo and look back toward the Cap Cana coast. You'll see the resort shoreline with the catamarans anchored offshore.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the calm water and shoreline. Go to 0.5x for more beach and sky, and try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out a catamaran.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and put the waterline on the lower third so the glassy water fills the frame, then tap the boats and drag it a touch darker if the sky is bright.
card.best_time: Early morning or late afternoon gives softer light and a quieter beach. Pick a still day, because calm water is what makes the reflections work.
card.selfie_here: Try the marina pool on the sunset side at Marina Cap Cana. Use the front camera with the pool and the sea entering the harbour behind you, and switch to 0.5x to fit more in.
card.ask_someone: At Plaza Marina, ask a passer-by to stand where the marina and yachts are in view, and pose with the water behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Cap Cana is a gated resort district, so some areas may need a visitor pass or be restricted. The Juanillo beach gate is only described as public during the day, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Zoom in on one catamaran and catch its reflection in the glassy water, with the waterline sitting right on a gridline.
card.good_to_know: Cap Cana covers roughly 123 square kilometres, so no single photo shows it all. Building began in the early 2000s. Punta Espada Golf Club, designed by Jack Nicklaus, opened in November 2006, and the first phase of Marina Cap Cana followed in 2007.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the shoreline of Playa Juanillo and look back toward the Cap Cana coast. You'll see the resort shoreline with the catamarans anchored offshore.

selfie_spots.why: The Princess Hotels guide describes the marina's pool water merging visually with the sea entering the port at sunset, which suits a selfie with the marina behind you.

selfie_research.notes: The sources do not name an exact selfie point with the Cap Cana landmark behind the visitor; the selfie spot is inferred from a marina pool/sunset description in a Princess Hotels blog that is about 7 years old. 'Cap Cana' is a large resort development, so I anchored the search to Marina Cap Cana, which is a judgement call. Playa Juanillo, between Cap Cana Marina and the Sanctuary resort, is named as a sunset beach by several sources, but no page gives a landmark-behind selfie position there, so I left it out. Hoyo Azul and Scape Park are inside Cap Cana but are separate attractions, not the landmark. No page states selfie stick or tripod rules, and no page gives a safety point for this landmark. The position coordinates were not matched to any named spot in the sources.
